title: Programme Office Ruling on the Ceiling for a Single Revaluation
content:
Ruling of the programme office on the Belrose Trade-In and Upgrade Programmes: the ceiling applied to the difference on a single revaluation of an issued credit is widened for a registration on which no revaluation has yet been booked, and the widening depends on how long ago the credit was issued.

## The ruling

Where no revaluation has yet been booked to the registration and the credit was issued within the last sixty (60) days, the ceiling is the whole of the credit already standing (100 percent of it). Where no revaluation has yet been booked to the registration but the credit was issued more than sixty days ago, the ceiling is two fifths of the credit already standing (40 percent of it). Where a revaluation has already been booked to the registration, no widening applies and the ceiling the desk publishes for one revaluation stands unchanged.

Whether a revaluation has been booked is read from the registration's entries: a revaluation entry standing among them means one has been booked. The days since issue are counted in calendar days from the issue date on the registration to the handling date.

## Both sides of each line

| Revaluation entries already on the registration | Days since the credit was issued | Ceiling |
|---|---|---|
| none | 60 or fewer | the whole of the credit already standing |
| none | 61 or more | two fifths of the credit already standing |
| one or more | any | the desk's published ceiling for one revaluation, unchanged |

A credit issued exactly 60 days ago is within the sixty days; one issued 61 days ago is not.

## Illustration on a hypothetical standing credit of 5000 USD

- No revaluation booked, credit issued 45 days ago: the ceiling is 5000.00 USD.
- No revaluation booked, credit issued 90 days ago: the ceiling is 2000.00 USD.
- A revaluation already booked, whenever the credit was issued: the desk's published ceiling for one revaluation, unchanged.
